advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard `policy.banked_ids()` calls inside the completion wrapper against `CompletionRecoveryError` (or make the read non-fail-loud) so a bad bank entry does not raise into the agent loop.
evidence: completion_banking.py:493-505 `all()` globs `self._dir` and calls `_read(path)` per entry
completion_banking.py:486-490 `_read` raises `CompletionRecoveryError` on an unrecognized/corrupt banked-verdict schema
advisory.finding: `policy.banked_ids()` resolves to `CriterionBank.all()`, which globs the bank directory and `_read`s every entry — a fail-loud operation that raises `CompletionRecoveryError` on a corrupt/unreadable/wrong-schema entry. It is now invoked inside the wrapper's `call_tool` under the lock on EVERY governed evidence or record call, so a bank read error propagates as an exception into the pydantic-ai agent loop instead of a graceful tool result. Previously the bank was only touched when the model explicitly recorded a verdict.
scenarios: A partially-written or schema-drifted bank entry exists when the model issues its next evidence call
Concurrent evidence batch each invoking banked_ids() under the lock

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document how a `CompletionRecoveryError` from `fallback_record` inside `call_tool` should be handled (swallow-and-return vs. propagate).
evidence: completion_tool_policy.py:89-90 `def fallback_record(...): return record_tool(criterion_id, False, evidence)`
completion_banking.py:446-470 `upsert` docstring 'Fail-loud on any write error.' and raises `CompletionRecoveryError` in the `except OSError` arm
advisory.finding: `fallback_record` calls `record_tool` -> `bank.upsert`, which is documented and implemented as fail-loud (raises `CompletionRecoveryError` on `OSError`). This raise now occurs inside the wrapper's `call_tool` after a successful evidence read at the bounded boundary, so a bank write failure aborts the run with an exception even though the underlying evidence tool call succeeded.
scenarios: Disk full / permission error when writing the bounded met=false verdict at the third evidence response

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the wrapper's third-call auto-bank with the prose contract (either fire the fallback only after a 4th attempted evidence call, or update the prompt so the model expects a met=false preemption on the 3rd result).
evidence: completion_tool_policy.py:166 `if target_id is not None and evidence_count >= policy.max_evidence_responses:` then `policy.fallback_record(target_id, BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE)`

completion_verifier.md:274-277 'Commit boundary: at count 3, the next response is commit. That response ... bank `met=true` when the evidence demonstrates the criterion, or bank `met=false` ... when it does not.'
advisory.finding: The wrapper force-banks `met=false` immediately when the third unique evidence response returns (`evidence_count >= max_evidence_responses`), but the authoritative system-prompt/state-machine contract states the model commits on the response AFTER count 3 and may bank `met=true` if that third result demonstrates the criterion. The wrapper therefore preempts the model's own commit of the third evidence result, and since a governed record cannot share the evidence step (COMMIT steering), the third result can never be committed as `met=true` in that step — it is banked `met=false` first.
scenarios: The third evidence read is exactly the read that demonstrates the criterion is MET

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'next response is commit' prompt/docstring wording with the code that auto-records met=false during the third evidence call.
evidence: completion_tool_policy.py: `if target_id is not None and evidence_count >= policy.max_evidence_responses:` then `policy.fallback_record(target_id, BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE)` executed within the same third `call_tool` invocation
completion_banking.py docstring: `The bounded transition enters COMMIT in the next response after the third repository evidence call.`
completion_verifier.md: `Commit boundary: **at count 3, the next response is commit.**`
advisory.finding: The reviewer prompt and record-tool docstring say the model gets a COMMIT response AFTER the third evidence call ('at count 3, the next response is commit'; 'enters COMMIT in the next response after the third repository evidence call'), but the policy code performs the bounded met=false fallback DURING the third evidence call itself (evidence_count >= max_evidence_responses), never yielding a next response for the model to commit.
scenarios: A dense criterion reaches the third evidence call; the model expects to commit on its next turn but the policy has already auto-banked met=false.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the prose-substring assertions in test_system_prompts_define_the_finite_per_criterion_bank_loop with behavioral coverage of the state machine, since the grepped strings are LLM-only prose that break on behavior-preserving rewording.
evidence: assert "at count 3, the next response is commit" in compact
search_files: the string 'at count 3, the next response is commit' appears only in completion_verifier.md, completion_banking.py (prompt/docstring text) and the test — no non-human parser consumes it
Rule-5 litmus: an LLM is NOT a non-human consumer; a prose grep guarding the author's wording is a change-detector
advisory.finding: test_system_prompts_define_the_finite_per_criterion_bank_loop asserts exact prose substrings of the completion_verifier.md reviewer prompt and successor_system_prompt (e.g. 'at count 3, the next response is commit', 'use applicable prefetched evidence first', 'every response in this loop contains exactly one tool call'). These strings are consumed only by the LLM, not by any parser/validator/registry that branches on the exact value (confirmed: they appear only in the prompt source and the test). This is a change-detector: it breaks on any behavior-preserving reword of the prompt with no observable behavior change, and does not verify the state-machine behavior (which is covered separately in test_completion_tool_policy.py).

advisory.finding: The concurrency-guard branch in wrap_completion_evidence_policy that SUPPRESSES the bounded fallback when the criterion was banked mid-flight (`if target_id not in set(policy.banked_ids())` after the awaited evidence call — 'A concurrently completed model record remains authoritative') has no test. test_third_unique_evidence_response_banks_bounded_fallback_before_return only covers the fallback FIRING; no test banks target_id between the third evidence claim and its await completion to assert the fallback is skipped.
